chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
That the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) forbade following a funeral with an incense burner.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on burning incense during a funeral procession in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s prohibition against following a funeral procession with an incense burner (mijmarah), reflecting the Shia emphasis on simplicity and avoiding ostentatious displays during burial rites. Scholars interpret this as a rejection of pre-Islamic customs of excessive mourning and decoration, aligning with the broader Islamic principle of modesty in death rituals. The ruling underscores the spiritual focus on the soul’s journey rather than material embellishments.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
that the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> forbade to follow the funeral pyre with burning incense’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Holy prophet, has said, ‘You must not walk behind the procession for a deceased with a brazier, censer.’”
